entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or self-hosted open-source software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight structures agent memory around retain, recall, and reflect operations. It supports hosted and local LLM providers, with deployment options including Docker, pip, and Kubernetes.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files. It supports scoped semantic search across directories and archives sessions into inspectable Markdown memories.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that gives agents persistent memory across sessions using a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It structures text into entities, relationships, and searchable chunks, and supports custom data models, plugins, and MCP.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts conversation facts, handles contradictions, and manages automatic forgetting. It also connects to services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports correcting or withdrawing them. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local; semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment are optional.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It tracks peers across workspaces and sessions, offers Python and TypeScript SDKs, and can run locally or be self-hosted.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git-managed repository, with version control for a context tree through commit, branch, and merge commands. It is an official Hermes Agent memory provider with a five-tier retrieval system, an interactive TUI and REPL, and support for 20 LLM providers.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents with one pure-Python dependency. It can integrate through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; its README reports BEAM results for v3.0.0 and marks LongMemEval as pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports exchanging memories through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search, structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and applies a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: AutoContext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents tackle complex tasks by running them against evaluations. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from that stored context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session histories across supported coding agents, helping users find past work and resume a session or continue it in another agent. Semantic recall is optional, and it runs without a model or server by default.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first layer for agent identity, memory, and secrets, with portable state across several agent harnesses and MCP clients. It connects through hooks, plugins, or extensions and includes a dashboard for browsing memory and asking questions.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memories as plain YAML files in an open engram format. It offers local search with keyword search as a fallback, plus a CLI and MCP server.
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory stores long-term memory locally in a SQLite file, using FTS5 search and a five-tier schema without a vector database or embeddings. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, including text and multimodal reordering for prefix-cache sharing. It integrates with Hermes Agent, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin provides explainable retrieval: each recall result includes a why_retrieved reason. It also supports memory canonicalization and contradiction tracking, with an embedded backend by default and an HTTP option.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn provides long-term, cross-project memory for coding agents, keeping durable memories as inspectable Markdown files in an Obsidian vault. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to agents.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven memory CLI maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history across sessions. It is designed to recall, maintain, and evolve knowledge without embeddings or a vector database.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-qmd uses an anticipatory cache that watches agent session logs to prefetch context. It combines local SQLite-vec storage with GGUF models via node-llama-cpp and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding-agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval. It provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep combines semantic search with BM25 full-text search and ranked graph traversal, while indexing codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support. Its edge tags link stored notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens through local keyword-based ranking and supports Tool Search. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible agents. Its workflows cover migrations, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations that are opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search with named relationships between entries. Importance-weighted recall prioritizes high-importance memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources, then registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports. It also registers hooks for pre-LLM calls and session end and finalization.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and a trace.jsonl audit log of prefetch operations. It supports immediate event deletion rather than retaining deleted events in persistent summaries.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and does not use a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: The XMemo plugin runs inside Hermes and communicates with XMemo over HTTPS to provide durable, cross-session memory with semantic search. It offers ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with slash commands for search, file reads, context, and Q&A. It supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, and includes repo sync and indexed git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers retrieval using HNSW ANN, sparse search, and an FM-index, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory-management and knowledge-graph traversal tools for Hermes Agent. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can automatically checkpoint context during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit curates agent memory stored in plain Markdown files, producing JSON diffs for review rather than using a database. Its “rot” and “lint” curators identify stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and lets you revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology whose skills trigger automatically in supported coding-agent harnesses. Its workflow covers specification, planning, and subagent-driven development, and the README provides installation instructions for multiple coding agents.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It supports coding-agent CLIs including Hermes Agent and includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project offers structured cybersecurity skills spanning 34 security domains, with mappings to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3 frameworks. Its stated compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms makes it a broad security-skills collection for agent users.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio diagrams. Its incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and it provides a diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills for agent-to-agent commerce, alongside vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds a verification and dispute-resolution layer.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid-ai-writing audits and rewrites content to address detectable AI-writing patterns, with rewrite mode supporting up to two editing passes. Its detector can score files or piped text, while in-place editing refuses source code, configuration, and generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw integrates with Hermes, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents to unify skills across agents and devices. Its dashboard covers skills, validation, versions, and session traces.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills, with compatibility for Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plugins.org specifications. It also maintains session state within the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection provides professional agent skills as plain Markdown files, with frameworks, templates, quality checks, and anti-patterns. It runs natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code, and the README documents installation and exports for other assistants.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube-skills provides skills for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It supports Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key with a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills, generating both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-hermes helps Hermes Agent generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks, with pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside an account of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, with progressive disclosure and remote skill registries sourced from Git or S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and script execution, with sandboxing to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that combine prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files from them with a tangler. Edits to source files can also be synced back into the literate document, making this skill useful for keeping code and documentation connected across agents.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design and implementation documents for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes suit different project complexities, and a PASS/FAIL review gate evaluates specs before handoff.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute approach. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, alongside CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares agent memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also includes a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models, tying retained work to model replacement.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Collects Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format and guides covering installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. Contributions are submitted through pull requests, making it a community resource for Portuguese-speaking Hermes users.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides official FLUX prompting guidance for image and video generation, plus BFL API integration with polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Offers nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills specification, for oracle network and smart contract interactions. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only and gives an npx command for installation.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with automated and step-by-step workflows. It also supports skill testing and export, covering creation through validation.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika is a workflow language for AI that checks workflows before calling a model and runs with a model of your choice. It also verifies a tamper-evident record for each run.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python SkilldockClient and a CLI. Its installation support resolves dependencies recursively, and it includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in rollback procedures provide a recovery path when execution needs to be reversed.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub provides a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills with one click. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.9 specification and federates search across GitHub and Hugging Face.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye narrows the skills presented to Hermes Agent using five retrieval layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings. This can reduce token usage before LLM calls, and the system degrades gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This skill creates reproducible VHS or Playwright recording scripts to add demo GIFs to a repository README. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, and can optimize GIFs to target sizes under 8 MB.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This project generates Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field drift.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches remoteopenclaw.com for more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. It integrates with MCP-compatible clients including Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This host-agnostic feedback loop fetches sessions, indexes installed skills, and drafts structured improvement proposals. Proposals are review-only by default, with an evaluation gate that supports deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage offers skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, along with packaged skills that combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. It also welcomes community contributions in `skills/community/`.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using path syntax for the current environment and select and verify existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. They support native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes skills to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, remove common Chinese AI writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extract structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. Its stated scope also includes OCR and e-commerce materials.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents list open support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for human review; public wallet earnings records are also available. Board creation returns a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests skill structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates that can be verified through its public API, which also accepts skill submissions.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, exposing 191 tools. It also includes five ready-to-use workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: AlphaPipeline provides quantitative risk checks for tokens, including honeypot, tax, and liquidity checks, and market data such as DEX slippage and funding rates. It offers both REST endpoints and a remote MCP server.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: This skill helps AI agents join KissCode through a one-call registration example. It also lists installation options for several agent platforms and provides a README badge snippet.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings across geographic scales, from global to street level, with core conclusions and action suggestions. It can also use user interests stored in semantic memory to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an astrology MCP endpoint with deterministic results and SHA-256 hashes for verification. The endpoint is listed as requiring no authentication, with per-call REST payment available through x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: A progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage while incrementally discovering server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon architecture maintains persistent connections, making it a distinctive skill for agents that need to work with MCP servers.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard reviews code for bugs using three parallel subagents focused on edge cases, adversarial review, and integration analysis, then consolidates and triages their findings. It also runs a deterministic pre-scan and can verify findings through proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox; it is read-only and does not fix code.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution OS for tracking recurring habits, which are scored daily, alongside tasks for other activities. It belongs on a Hermes Agent skills list because it connects to agents over MCP and includes an Android client, while keeping data local in SQLite.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill uses three parallel agents—Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness—to simplify code in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust. Its tiered application process includes an approval gate, making it a fit for teams that want code simplification with review before changes are applied.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: A turnkey cybersecurity lab for Hermes Agent, with 397 CVE-driven skills and 152 tools, including tools for network security, forensics, and exploitation. Its 28 integrated cybersecurity frameworks and standards make it a broad option for adding security-focused capabilities to Hermes Agent.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts fablize’s verified procedures, including multi-story task decomposition with mandatory evidence-based verification gates. It also provides an investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state management—making it a focused skill for structured, evidence-grounded work.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: PederHP/skillsdotnet is a C#/.NET implementation of agentskills.io that uses SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories, making it a fit for Hermes Agent setups that need skill discovery and loading in .NET.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time observability dashboard for Hermes Agent, bringing together session history, skill analytics, token costs, and operational details such as health, cron, channels, errors, and incidents. It belongs in this list for its read-only, local-first approach with log desensitization, plus optional incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: A collection of plain Markdown skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode, with workflows for code review and session management. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer, making this a practical addition to a list of reusable agent skills.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix project packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and automatically updates its packages daily. Its README provides `nix run` commands for the listed tools, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to device hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This project provides a Termux installer and guide for running Hermes Agent on Android, using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models through Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct and CRD-based deployment workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image with mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first web control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances, each with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This project provides a Helm chart for running Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation options via an OCI registry or a published Helm repository. Provider-specific values examples and CI installation on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a deployment option with documented configuration examples and a Kubernetes install check.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local, pre-indexed project graph with `codegraph init` and auto-syncs it as files change. Its MCP server connects the graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, with the stated goal of reducing token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale is a CLI for tracking token usage across AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini. It also provides a visualization dashboard for analyzing usage, making it useful for comparing activity across clients.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for coding-agent API traffic, including prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage. It can compare adjacent requests to show context changes and redacts common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools. It reads Hermes Agent usage from its state database and includes historical trends and usage breakdowns.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design skills, UI prompts, and layout guidance to help build interfaces with AI. It connects to coding tools through TypeUI MCP or plugins and supports AI providers that accept Markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an installable workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It includes product development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop with seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for skins and themes for the Hermes terminal UI. Users can create skins with YAML files, and custom skins inherit unspecified values from the default skin.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks agent-facing content, including configurations, tool descriptions, and system prompts, using HERM v1.1 scoring. Its findings include file locations and suggested fixes, and it supports CI gates and reviewed baselines.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce using Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser designed for autonomous agent control via MCP. It supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows, with a supervisor sidebar for managing approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs natively without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized around two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin auto-captures and auto-recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for token-saving CLI workflows, with a stated 90–99% token savings. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, plus automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes Agents with per-folder configuration and skills. It can switch between default and scoped agents, with project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of hermes-agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes Agent. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: observeco is a self-healing observability tool for AI agents, with a native Hermes plugin that exports real-time conversation telemetry. Its monitoring offers zero-token passive analysis or scheduled active probing, and uses config-aware baselines to detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with offline operation that requires no API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro, along with adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup provides a deterministic, zero-network local runtime by default, with explicit approval required for consequential actions and external writes. It includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: This Hermes memory plugin supports semantic search and multidimensional memory storage. It provides tools to search, add, and delete memories, and includes a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC-Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. It stands out for one-click API provider switching and a central place to manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that does not require a separate CLI installation. It also includes 21 built-in professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides web and phone access to Hermes Agent through a three-panel layout for sessions, chat, and workspace files. Its file browser offers inline previews, and the project is designed for access through an SSH tunnel.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for Hermes Agent that brings together chats, sessions, agent integrations, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also supports visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, or Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace is a web workspace combining chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel. Its highlights include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a workspace file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that gathers sessions from Hermes and other agents in a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees; it includes 19 agents and supports ACP agents.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH, using real session data and a real terminal. It provides native views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs, along with an embedded terminal for shell access and system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, with support for Windows and macOS and native window and process management. Its interface includes chat, memory management, and LaTeX/Markdown rendering, while its built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel provides health checks and updates.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted remote connections. Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats, while Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It can stream chats and attach files or images, browse and resume server sessions, and show scheduled tasks, skills, memory, and insights.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, and its live workspace monitors code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes for monitoring agent growth, Git projects, and scheduled cron jobs. Its tmux operator view also helps users manage live agent panes, making it a fit for hands-on terminal-based workspace management.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS session browser brings together session search, agent activity, and analytics for Hermes and other coding-agent CLIs. It can search prompts, tool activity, errors, and file paths, track Codex and Claude quota burn per session, and build its search index locally.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard provides a browser-based workspace for the Hermes AI agent stack, with a terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel. Its real-time chat, MCP server controls, and ZOO Swarm Monitor add tools for interaction and agent oversight.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: Hermes Desktop OS1 is a native macOS workspace for running Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts. It offers one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers and integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent to web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects before they proceed.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also includes a kanban board for agentic work, plus controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run React SPA provides a 10-page, mobile-first dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its features include streaming terminal chat with file attachments, Telegram validation using dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication, and background agent spawning for up to five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent is a Windows desktop version with a dark-themed, multilingual GUI and session management. It supports local models through LM Studio and includes workflow automation and runtime tool creation.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a self-hosted AI assistant interface with a glassmorphic design, chat, and real-time log streaming. Its file browser and task dashboard sit alongside management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: This dashboard focuses on monitoring Hermes processes and configuration, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also supports inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, while keeping configuration and environment-variable views read-only.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan UI is a self-hosted AI workspace organized around chat, with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. It also provides a marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, plus isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client brings together streaming chat, model switching, and collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents. Its visual Skill Store offers 50+ curated one-click installations, alongside a PM orchestrator.
entries.nicolasestrem/hermes-model-switcher: A plugin for the Hermes Agent Web Dashboard that displays configured routes across profiles in one matrix. It previews changes before applying them and includes named presets and guarded Undo, making cross-profile model switching easier to review and reverse.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: An unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent, available on Android, web, macOS, and Linux alpha. It adds command approvals, live tool-step updates, and interactive answer cards for checklists, choices, forms, rankings, and votes.
